groups.rule: asOf — the value in effect on a given day. The runner builds a fixed two-entry series of its own (2010-01-01 -> "A", 2011-01-04 -> "B") rather than reading f8n's data, so these cases pin the lookup's semantics and stay true when the tax history is extended. A day the series does not cover is reported as "(none)": it is a defined outcome, not a rejected input, and encoding it as an error would conflate the two.

cases.note: The rule the whole type turns on: a value effective FROM a date applies ON that date. Off by one here and every rate is wrong for exactly one day, in one language.
The other side of the same boundary — the previous entry is still in effect.
Inclusive at the start of the series too.
The newest entry stands indefinitely; the type never extrapolates past it.
No answer, rather than the oldest known value. Returning "A" here would be a wrong number that looks like a right one.
